{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}}
'''Robert Neville Haszeldine'''  [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry|FRSC]]  (3 May 1925 &ndash; 13 October 2016) was a British [[chemist]]. He is best known for his contributions to [[organofluorine chemistry]], such as the discovery/invention of [[triflic acid]].<ref>{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PKegfJ_fVBMC&q=Robert+Haszeldine+manchester&pg=PA63| title=Fluorine chemistry at the millennium: fascinated by fluorine| author=Ronald Eric Banks| publisher=Elsevier|year= 2000| isbn=978-0-08-043405-6}}</ref>

==Life==
He was educated at [[Stockport Grammar School]] and the [[University of Birmingham]].
Moving to the [[University of Cambridge]] he rose to assistant director of Research,<ref>{{cite book| url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PKegfJ_fVBMC&q=Robert+Haszeldine+manchester&pg=PA63| title=Fluorine chemistry at the millennium: fascinated by fluorine| author=Ronald Eric Banks| publisher=Elsevier|year= 2000| isbn=978-0-08-043405-6}}</ref> before becoming Professor of Chemistry and Principal of the [[University of Manchester Institute of Science and Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.queens.cam.ac.uk/Queens/Misc/Fellows/1900-99.html | title=Fellows 1900–1999 &#124; Queens' College}}</ref>

He had a two-acre garden in [[Great Langdale]], Cumbria, which was regularly opened to the public under the [[National Garden Scheme]].<ref>[http://www.english-lakes.com/garden_copt_howe.htm Copt Howe]</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.independent.co.uk/travel/uk/hail-the-glory-of-an-english-country-garden-489743.html | location=London | work=The Independent | date=27 March 2005 | title=Hail the glory of an English country garden}}</ref>

He was elected Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 1968.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Munn|first1=R. W.|last2=Taylor|first2=D. R.|date=2019|title=Robert Neville Haszeldine. 3 May 1925—13 October 2016|journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society|volume=66|pages=243–265|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2018.0035|doi-access=free}}</ref>

He died on 13 October 2016 at the age of 91.<ref>[http://www.stockportgrammar.co.uk/death/robert-haszeldine/ Robert Haszeldine (OS 1942)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220115814/http://www.stockportgrammar.co.uk/death/robert-haszeldine/ |date=20 December 2016 }} Stockport Grammar school</ref>
